C5^3 encoding independently re-derived in verifier (720 injections Z5->{0..5}, 5 consecutive-triple edges, asserted 5 distinct). Cross-checks: labeled distribution sums to 371229; m=0..4 entries equal C(20,m)=1,20,190,1140,4845 as required since C5 needs 5 edges; type counts per m sum to 835; unique 13-edge type has orbit 60 dividing 720 with degrees (6,6,7,7,7,6) as stated; 12-edge orbits 90+45+15+180+360+360+15=1065 match. This is exhaustive-enumeration proof (computational certificate), not asymptotic argument, and is honestly scoped to n=6 with no pi(C5^3) claim.

originality.rationale: Correctness-verified exact unrestricted n=6 single-C5^3 census (371229 labeled / 835 types / E6=13 with unique extremal) is not stated or implied in any checked prior. BLLP arXiv:2506.03223 settles only the pair {C4^3,C5^3} and single l>=7 not divisible by 3 at density 2*sqrt(3)-3 with stability, explicitly excluding single C5^3, and gives asymptotic/SDP results, never a 6-vertex type census or E6 value. KLP arXiv:2209.08134 determines pi only for large l not divisible by 3 and records the Mubayi-Rodl 2*sqrt(3)-3 lower-bound conjecture for C5, no finite-order census. Admission-cited Balogh-Luo / Lidicky-Mattes-Pfender concern the distinct minus-one-edge family at density 1/4. Nearest census prior (SCOPE-internal SCOPE064, per admission record) is explicitly shifted-only on 7 vertices (352 ideals / 68 C5-free / max 16) and disclaims asymptotics; it neither covers nor mechanically implies the unrestricted n=6 classification, since C5-containment on 6 vertices is a global property. No timestamp or failed search was used as proof; comparison is substantive (asymptotic vs exact census; shifted-restricted vs unrestricted).
